content:
The image shows green banana fruits with a distinctive dark brown-to-black necrotic rot at the distal tips (the ends away from the bunch). The rot appears dry and extends inward from the tip, giving the affected ends a burnt/charred appearance — classic for Cigar End Rot caused by *Verticillium theobromae*.

Ruling out other classes:
- **Bunchy Top, Panama Disease, Cordana Leaf Spot, Yellow & Black Sigatoka**: all manifest on leaves/stems, not fruit tips.
- **Anthracnose**: causes dark sunken lesions on ripening fruit surfaces, often with salmon/orange sporulation — not tip-specific.

The tip-confined, dry, blackened rot on green fruits is the hallmark of **Cigar End Rot**.
